subject: Renewal: Q3 committed GPU ramp + tier consolidation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@atlasai.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlasai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Q3 committed GPU ramp + tier consolidation

Hi Sarah / Raj —

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is a proposal for Atlas AI's upcoming renewal window covering the next 12 months. Instead of the four distinct GPU tiers you're currently running, we modeled a consolidated two-tier commit (Base + Burst) that should reduce per-token unit cost while simplifying ops. Key points: 

- Base layer: 32 GPUs reserved (mixed A100/RTX depending on region) for steady-state throughput; predictable monthly spend.
- Burst buffer: 8 GPUs reserved for short-lived peaks with agreed throttling/fallback rules.
- Throughput guarantee: we propose a 99th percentile per-request latency SLO and a monthly throughput floor expressed as tokens/minute for each route (see workbook).
- Mid-term uplift option at 6 months to add blocks of 8 GPUs with pre-negotiated pricing.

I've included two pricing scenarios in the PDF (Consolidated-Standard and Consolidated-Premium with a 12% discount in exchange for a 12-month commit and a 30% longer billing cadence). Would like to run through this with you tomorrow — are you available 10–11am PT?

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Proposal_Q3_GPU_Consolidation_v3.pdf)
From: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@atlasai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlasai.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Q3 committed GPU ramp + tier consolidation

Thanks Jonas — reviewed the deck. A few quick asks from our side before we lock time: 

1) Can you map the Base layer to our existing critical routes (embed-index, candidate-rerank) and show expected p95 latency under our QPS patterns? The workbook mentions tokens/min but we need endpoint-level guarantees.
2) We need a firm mid-term uplift price cap; if commodity prices rise we can't accept open-ended increases. Can you commit to a max uplift rate?
3) If we move to a consolidated model, what happens to the historical billing credits we've accrued under the current multi-tier pool? Need clarity on credit application.

Also — our procurement has a hard requirement for a one-time onboarding credit if we lock 12 months early. Is that something Redwood can include?

Can take the 10am PT slot tomorrow.

—Sarah
Sarah Collins
Head of ML Platforms, Atlas AI
(Attachment: Atlas_Renewal_worksheet.xlsx)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@atlasai.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlasai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 12:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Q3 committed GPU ramp + tier consolidation

Sarah — appreciate the clarity, good questions. Short answers up front: 

- Endpoint mapping: yes, we'll provide an endpoint-level throughput & latency appendix. I've looped in Lauren (solutions) and Marcus (pricing) to validate the p95 modeling against your traffic trace.
- Mid-term uplift cap: we can agree to a capped uplift formula: base uplift per-GPU + marketplace surcharge cap not to exceed 6% per uplift event, max two uplift events in the 12-month term. I'll have Marcus confirm the exact numbers.
- Credits: any unused credits tied to your current pools will be pro-rated and applied to the first billing cycle under the new consolidated commit. We'll include a short clause in the amendment.
- Onboarding credit: we typically offer a 1-month onboarding credit for early 12-month commits; happy to include that on the Standard consolidated plan.

I'll bring an updated workbook and a polished term-sheet to the call. See you at 10am PT.

Best,
Jonas
(Attachment: Throughput_Guarantee_Workbook.xlsx)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: Q3 committed GPU ramp + tier consolidation — please advise on SLA caps and uplift pricing

Folks — forwarding Atlas AI thread. They want endpoint-level p95 projections, a hard cap on mid-term uplift pricing, and confirmation on credit handling. Short checklist below: 

- Lauren: can you run the embed-index / candidate-rerank traces through our p95 model and produce a short appendix showing expected latencies at 32+8 topology and at 40 consolidated? Include assumptions (batch sizes, KV cache hit rates).
- Marcus: confirm uplift cap language (I proposed max 6% per uplift event, max 2 events). If we can give a slightly tighter cap (4.5%) in exchange for a 9-month notice window we might protect margin — propose both options.
- Legal/Finance: we need wording for pro-rating legacy credits to new commit and onboarding credit application.

Low urgency but would like a response by EOD Thu so I can update the workbook before the pricing call next week.

Thanks —
Jonas
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Collins <sarah.collins@atlasai.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlasai.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Q3 committed GPU ramp + tier consolidation — uplift cap and SLA language

Hi all — following up with the agreed wording and numbers after internal review. Posting final terms here so we have a single source-of-truth before we push for signature: 

1) Uplift pricing cap: 5% per uplift event on the per-GPU committed rate. Clients may request up to two uplift events in a rolling 12-month term. Atlas may exercise a third uplift in exceptional cases subject to mutual written agreement.

2) Onboarding credit: Redwood will apply a 1x monthly credit applied to the first invoice for customers that convert to a 12-month consolidated commit and sign within 30 days of proposal acceptance.

3) Throughput & latency appendix: see attached workbook tab 'Endpoint-SLA' (summary): we guarantee p95 latency for embed-index <= 220ms and candidate-rerank <= 310ms at the specified 32 GPU Base (assumes KV cache hit >= 65% and batching policy B-2). If Atlas requires >80% KV hit-rate guarantees, we need an addendum due to higher engineering support and QA.

4) Credit handling: All historical credits tied to legacy pools will be pro-rated and applied to the first invoice under the new consolidated plan. Any disputes about past credits must be raised within 30 days of activation.

I'll attach the finalized workbook and updated term sheet for Atlas's procurement/legal review. If this looks good to you Sarah, we can request signature and issue DocuSign.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Proposal_Q3_GPU_Consolidation_v3.pdf, Attachment: Throughput_Guarantee_Workbook.xlsx)
